segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
My name is Marco.
My name is Catherine and today we're talking a little bit about small talk.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们谈谈闲聊。

segments.en: That's right.
We are getting towards the end of our series.
segments.zh: 我们的系列节目快到尾声了。

segments.en: Actually this is the last podcast that we will have all about small talk and we're just going to be following Mr. Campbell and Michelle and Melissa and they're just going to talk very briefly about the weather, about traveling, very casual things.
segments.zh: 实际上，这是我们最后一期关于闲聊的播客，我们将跟随坎贝尔先生、米歇尔和梅丽莎，他们只会非常简短地聊聊天气、旅行这些非常随意的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
So let's take a listen to this dialogue and we'll be back in a moment to discuss what's going on.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听听这个对话，我们稍后会回来讨论正在发生的事情。

segments.en: Hi ladies.
Thanks for picking me up.
It's awful weather out there.
Absolutely.
It's been raining for hours.
segments.zh: 已经下了好几个小时的雨了。

segments.en: How are you Melissa?
Are you okay?
I'm great thanks Mr. Campbell.
segments.zh: 我很好，谢谢您，坎贝尔先生。

segments.en: Do you have any business trips planned soon, Mr. Campbell?
segments.zh: 坎贝尔先生，您近期有出差安排吗？

segments.en: Of course.
I'm always traveling.
I'm leaving for London next Monday and then I'll fly to Boston from there.
segments.zh: 下周一我去伦敦，然后从那里飞去波士顿。

segments.en: It's going to be a busy month.
How about you Michelle?
Do you have any vacation plans?
Yes.
Mike and I will travel to Beijing to see Mike's parents for the Spring Festival, and hopefully next year we will visit London.
segments.zh: 迈克和我春节会去北京看望他的父母，希望明年还能去伦敦。

segments.en: I hear it's a wonderful city.
segments.zh: 听说那是一座很棒的城市。

segments.en: I couldn't agree more.
London is really fantastic.
It's my favorite city.
I'm sure you'll have a great time.
All right.
We're back.
So now let's take a look at language takeaway.
All right.
We don't have that much today in language takeaway but we do have a couple of really important words and phrases.
segments.zh: 我们今天在语言要点方面没有那么多，但我们确实有几个非常重要的单词和短语。

segments.en: The first one comes from the very first line.
Mr. Campbell says, hi ladies.
segments.zh: 坎贝尔先生说，嗨，女士们。

segments.en: Thanks for picking me up.
That's right.
Now this phrasal verb, to pick someone up, means to get them, right?
segments.zh: 这个短语动词 pick someone up 的意思是去接某人，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, to gather them, to collect them.
segments.zh: 是的，就是去接他们，把他们接上。

segments.en: You can do this with a car like I will pick you up at the airport.
segments.zh: 你可以用一辆车来做这件事，就像我会在机场接你一样。

segments.en: But you can also do it in person by just walking to a place and meeting somebody and then taking them somewhere else.
segments.zh: 但你也可以亲自走到一个地方和某人见面，然后把他们带到其他地方来做。

segments.en: That's the important part.
You take them somewhere else.
So maybe if you go pick your kids up from school, you just walk there, you get them and you walk back home.
segments.zh: 所以也许如果你去学校接孩子，你只要走到那里，接上他们，然后一起走回家。

segments.en: That's right.
And so the key here is that you remember that the verb goes first, I will pick and then you have the person.
segments.zh: 所以这里的关键是，动词在前：I will pick，后面再接人。

segments.en: I will pick you up.
I will pick them up.
He will pick us up.
That's right.
So the subject goes between pick and up.
segments.zh: 所以人称代词要放在 pick 和 up 之间。

segments.en: That's right.
All right.
So we're going to pick someone up.
And then Mr. Campbell comments on the weather.
segments.zh: 然后坎贝尔先生评论天气。

segments.en: He says it's awful weather out there.
segments.zh: 他说外面的天气很糟糕。

segments.en: It's awful.
All right.
So awful, you listen to the tone, you automatically think that this is probably a bad thing.
segments.zh: 太糟糕了，你听着语气，你自然而然地认为这可能是一件坏事。

segments.en: And you're right, it is a bad thing.
segments.zh: 你是对的，这是一件坏事。

segments.en: But what's another way to say awful?
segments.zh: 但形容 awful 还有别的说法吗？

segments.en: It's terrible.
It's bad.
It's horrible.
So awful is a way to say something's really bad.
segments.zh: 所以 awful 就是形容某事非常糟糕的一个词。

segments.en: And we use it very often with the weather.
segments.zh: 我们经常用它来形容天气。

segments.en: This weather is awful.
But we can also use it about other things like food, for example.
segments.zh: 但我们也可以将它用于其他东西，例如食物。

segments.en: So if you have something to eat and it doesn't taste good, you can say this is awful.
segments.zh: 所以如果你有东西吃，但味道不好，你可以说这很糟糕。

segments.en: What is this?
Or what's that awful smell?
segments.zh: 或者那是什么难闻的气味？

segments.en: Oh, Marco took his shoes off.
Right, an awful smell.
All right.
And well, Mr. Campbell went on to tell them that he's taking another trip soon, but a specific kind of trip.
segments.zh: 好吧，坎贝尔先生接着告诉他们，他很快就要去一次旅行了，但又是一种特定的旅行。

segments.en: All right.
So you know that there are many different kinds of trips, but the one that he's taking is a business trip.
segments.zh: 所以你知道有许多不同类型的旅行，但他要去的是一次商务旅行。

segments.en: So normally we could just say I'm going on a trip next year.
segments.zh: 所以通常我们可以说我明年要去旅行。

segments.en: But here we specify, we say it's a business trip.
segments.zh: 但在这里我们指定，我们说这是一次商务旅行。

segments.en: So what are we doing on this trip, Marco?
segments.zh: 那么，我们在这次旅行中做什么，马可呢？

segments.en: That's right.
So we're basically working.
segments.zh: 所以我们基本上在工作。

segments.en: We're going because our company needs us to go to a meeting or to do some work abroad.
segments.zh: 我们要去是因为我们公司需要我们去参加会议或在国外做一些工作。

segments.en: All right.
So you know on a business trip that you'll be doing work things, you'll be having meetings, you will not be going to Disney World, you will not be meeting with friends and going to movies probably.
segments.zh: 所以你知道在商务旅行中你会做工作，你会开会，你不会去迪斯尼世界，你可能不会和朋友见面，也不会去看电影。

segments.en: Right, exactly.
So it's very different from a vacation.
A vacation you go with the objective of going to these fun places.
segments.zh: 一个假期，你的目的是去这些有趣的地方。

segments.en: So can I say I'm going on a business vacation?
segments.zh: 那我能说我要去“商务度假”吗？

segments.en: No, you're either going on vacation or you're taking a business trip.
segments.zh: 不，你要么去度假，要么要出差。

segments.en: All right, business trip.
So now let's take a break and let's review our dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们休息一下，让我们回顾一下我们的对话。

segments.en: Hi, ladies.
Thanks for picking me up.
It's awful weather out there.
Absolutely.
It's been raining for hours.
segments.zh: 已经下了好几个小时的雨了。

segments.en: How are you, Melissa?
Are you okay?
I'm great, thanks, Mr. Campbell.
segments.zh: 我很好，谢谢，坎贝尔先生。

segments.en: Do you have any business trips planned soon, Mr. Campbell?
segments.zh: 坎贝尔先生，您近期有出差安排吗？

segments.en: Of course, I'm always traveling.
I'll leave for London next Monday and then I'll fly to Boston from there.
segments.zh: 我将在下周一启程前往伦敦，然后我将从那里飞往波士顿。

segments.en: It's going to be a busy month.
How about you, Michelle?
Do you have any vacation plans?
Yes, Mike and I will travel to Beijing to see Mike's parents for the spring festival and hopefully next year we will visit London.
segments.zh: 是的，迈克和我将前往北京看迈克的父母过春节，希望明年我们能去伦敦。

segments.en: I hear it's a wonderful city.
segments.zh: 听说那是一座很棒的城市。

segments.en: I couldn't agree more.
London is really fantastic.
It's my favorite city.
I'm sure you'll have a great time.
All right, so now let's take a look at four key phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在让我们来看看关于流利表达的四个关键短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
All right, now we have a great phrase for everybody here in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在我们在流利表达中为每个人提供了一个很棒的短语。

segments.en: Melissa is talking to Mr. Campbell and he asks her how she is.
segments.zh: 梅丽莎正在和坎贝尔先生说话，他问她怎么样。

segments.en: Are you okay?
And she says, I'm great, thanks.
Now Marco, why would we use this phrase instead of I'm fine, thank you?
segments.zh: 现在马可，我们为什么要用这句话而不是我很好，谢谢？

segments.en: Well, it's basically the same thing.
It's just another way of answering this common question, how are you?
segments.zh: 这只是回答这个常见问题的另一种方式，你好吗？

segments.en: You can say I'm fine, thank you.
I'm well.
But this is just another way of saying I'm okay.
segments.zh: 但这只是说我没事的另一种方式。

segments.en: All right, but I think it's important too to remember that this is also very casual like the rest of the conversation and pretty enthusiastic.
segments.zh: 好吧，但我认为重要的是要记住，这也很随意，就像其他谈话一样，非常热情。

segments.en: She's great.
So, it's important to remember that I'm fine, thanks is standard, it's very normal, but I'm great is a nice way to change it and do something different.
segments.zh: 所以，重要的是要记住我很好，谢谢是标准的，这很正常，但我很棒是改变它和做一些不同的事情的好方法。

segments.en: That's right.
Okay.
And now we wanted to ask if we have any plans, but we wanted to know if we have any vacation plans.
segments.zh: 现在我们想问我们是否有任何计划，但我们想知道我们是否有任何假期计划。

segments.en: And the interesting thing about this question was that Mr. Campbell said, any vacation plans?
segments.zh: 这个问题的有趣之处在于坎贝尔先生说，有什么假期计划吗？

segments.en: So that's the whole sentence.
Well, first he says, how about you, Michelle?
segments.zh: 好吧，首先他说，你呢，米歇尔？

segments.en: Any vacation plans?
So what we think here is that maybe it's wrong.
segments.zh: 我们可能会觉得这样说不对。

segments.en: Do you have any vacation plans is something that we'd want to hear, right?
segments.zh: 你有什么假期计划是我们想听的，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
But here we don't actually need to say, do you have any vacation plans?
segments.zh: 但在这里我们实际上不需要说，你有什么假期计划吗？

segments.en: Because it's pretty clear who we're talking to.
segments.zh: 因为很清楚我们在和谁说话。

segments.en: We're talking to Michelle, right?
segments.zh: 我们在和米歇尔说话，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
And we're talking about traveling and we're talking about plans.
segments.zh: 我们正在谈论旅行，我们正在谈论计划。

segments.en: So it's overstated that we don't really need to say, do you have any vacation plans?
segments.zh: 所以这其实有点多余，我们并不真的需要说“你有什么假期计划吗？”

segments.en: We're already talking about the subject.
segments.zh: 我们已经在谈论这个话题了。

segments.en: Now, this is a great way to transition.
segments.zh: 现在，这是一个很好的过渡方式。

segments.en: One person is talking about himself or herself and then you want to talk about the other person.
segments.zh: 一个人在谈论他自己，然后你想谈论另一个人。

segments.en: So you say, what about you?
Any vacation plans or any dinner plans or any ideas?
segments.zh: 任何假期计划或任何晚餐计划或任何想法？

segments.en: Exactly.
So it's a great way to, like you say, transition from one idea or from one person to another.
segments.zh: 因此，就像您说的那样，这是一种从一个想法或一个人过渡到另一个人的好方法。

segments.en: Now to the next phrase, a very common one, and specifically when you are not really sure about something, but somebody told you.
segments.zh: 现在到下一个短语，一个非常常见的短语，特别是当你不确定某事时，但有人告诉你。

segments.en: Specifically in this case, Michelle says, I hear it's a wonderful city when talking about London.
segments.zh: 特别是在这种情况下，米歇尔说，在谈论伦敦时，我听说这是一个很棒的城市。

segments.en: So what does she mean by I hear it's a wonderful city?
segments.zh: 那么她说我听说这是一个美妙的城市是什么意思？

segments.en: Well basically Michelle is saying she's never been to London, but she's read or she's heard from friends or from a TV show that London's a wonderful city.
segments.zh: 好吧，基本上米歇尔是在说她从未去过伦敦，但她从朋友那里听说过，或者从电视节目里看到过，说伦敦是座很棒的城市。

segments.en: So she can't say it is a wonderful city because she's never been there, but she can say, listen, you know, I have, I have heard this from other people or from magazines.
segments.zh: 所以她不能说这是一个美妙的城市，因为她从未去过那里，但她可以说，听着，你知道，我有，我从其他人或杂志上听到过这个消息。

segments.en: So it's not even clear where she heard it, but that's not really important.
segments.zh: 所以还不清楚她在哪里听到的，但这并不重要。

segments.en: So basically the idea is that we don't know personally, but we have friends that told us or we have read in a magazine or a TV show, we've seen it, that it's great.
segments.zh: 所以基本上就是，我们不是亲身了解，而是听朋友说的，或者在杂志、电视节目上看到过，说它很棒。

segments.en: So you can use it with many things like a restaurant.
segments.zh: 所以这个说法可以用在很多东西上，比如餐厅。

segments.en: That's right.
I hear the food is delicious.
Or I could say, hey Marco, I'm going to Hong Kong Disneyland next year.
segments.zh: 或者我可以说，嘿，马可，明年我要去香港迪士尼乐园。

segments.en: Right.
And I can say, oh, I hear that it's a very fun place.
segments.zh: 我可以说，哦，我听说这是一个非常有趣的地方。

segments.en: So Marco, you've never been there, right?
segments.zh: 所以马可，你从来没有去过那里，对吧？

segments.en: No, I've never been there.
segments.zh: 不，我从来没有去过那里。

segments.en: Okay.
All right.
And to finish off, Mr. Campbell agrees completely about London being such a wonderful city.
segments.zh: 最后，坎贝尔先生完全同意伦敦是一座如此美妙的城市。

segments.en: And he says, I couldn't agree more.
I couldn't agree more.
So he agrees.
We understand that.
But I couldn't agree more is like saying, I really, really agree.
segments.zh: 但 I couldn't agree more 就好像在说：我真的、真的非常同意。

segments.en: Right.
Like you are completely right.
Yeah.
So this is a way to exaggerate.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种夸张的方式。

segments.en: You know, you want to say, I agree.
Eh, it's a little boring.
So you say, I couldn't agree more.
I'm agreeing the most I can.
segments.zh: 我已经同意到不能再同意了。

segments.en: That's right.
And then we can also use the opposite, which would be if you disagree with someone.
segments.zh: 然后我们也可以使用相反的情况，如果您不同意某人的观点。

segments.en: I couldn't disagree more.
So you just change that one word.
I couldn't disagree more.
So maybe I don't like London.
segments.zh: 所以也许我不喜欢伦敦。

segments.en: Maybe it's too rainy or too dark for me.
segments.zh: 也许对我来说雨太多，或者太阴暗了。

segments.en: So I say, I couldn't disagree more.
segments.zh: 所以我说，我完全不同意。

segments.en: I think London is terrible.
Maybe not the right thing to say in a small talk situation, but we can talk about that in a minute.
segments.zh: 在闲聊的情况下也许不是正确的说法，但我们可以在一分钟内讨论一下。

segments.en: Exactly.
All right.
So let's review everything one last time.
segments.zh: 所以让我们最后一次回顾一下一切。

segments.en: Hi, ladies.
Thanks for picking me up.
It's awful weather out there.
Absolutely.
It's been raining for hours.

I'm great.
Thanks, Mr. Campbell.
Do you have any business trips planned soon, Mr. Campbell?

segments.en: Of course.
I'm always traveling.
I'm leaving for London next Monday, and then I'll fly to Boston from there.

We've gotten some great feedback about the different topics and small conversations you can have with a stranger, a co-worker, a friend, to kind of not have that awkward silence.
segments.zh: 我们收到了一些不错的反馈，讲的都是你可以和陌生人、同事、朋友聊的不同话题和简短对话，以免出现那种尴尬的沉默。

We've gone over a lot of different situations.
segments.zh: 我们经历了很多不同的情况。
